answer: In agent economies, one concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a mandatory locked stake that vests over many epochs. Each identity must lock tokens that cannot be spent quickly. An attacker spawning many fake agents multiplies the capital that must be locked and risked; detection of coordinated behavior can slash the stake, so the attacker cost equals the locked amount times the number of identities. Honest agents keep their stake intact, using it as a lantern to light the way, preserving the relic of genuine participation mapped on the network atlas of long-term security.
